key_insight: Hybrid Cinematography combines physical filming with generative video reshooting so directors can preview and manage hallucination risk before it becomes a costly problem. It turns a post-production uncertainty into something that can be evaluated and addressed while the crew is still on set.
problem_solved: Generative video reshooting can require inventing unseen or unrecorded content, and those hallucination gaps are often discovered too late, after leaving the set. This paper addresses the need to detect and mitigate that risk during production.
method: Uses an editable 3D shot plan to represent the intended camera move and scene structure.
Combines the shot plan with a proxy of the actual take to previsualize how reshooting will behave.
Evaluates hallucination risk during previsualization so filmmakers can adjust the plan while changes are still possible.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shows how generative video tools can be integrated into real production workflows with risk-aware feedback loops. It provides a practical framework for making generative systems more usable, controllable, and production-ready.
visual_elements: A side-by-side of the real filmed take and the generative reshot version
A workflow diagram showing capture -> proxy -> previsualization -> risk assessment -> adjustment
A 3D shot-plan interface with editable camera path arrows
A highlighted risk map marking regions likely to require hallucination
paper_title: Hybrid Cinematography: Previsualizing and Managing Hallucination Risk in Generative Video Reshooting
paper_authors: Nhan,  Tran, Neal Wadhwa, Abe Davis, Stefan Stojanov
